 NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Garrett Wilson cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol and will play in Week 10 against the Bills.
 Wilson missed Week 9 because of the concussion but has cleared the league’s concussion protocol ahead of today’s game. Jets coach Aaron Glenn told reporters on Friday he expected Wilson to play, so this doesn’t come as much of a surprise. In a potential shootout with the Bills, Wilson will push for a high-end WR2 designation this week. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak 
 Source:  Ian Rapoport

 Garrett Wilson (concussion) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bills. 
 All three of the Jets’ starting wide receivers are questionable to play, though Wilson practiced in full practice and is expected to play. Wilson could handle a hefty workload if he is indeed cleared to play, as expected, and one or two of the others are limited or ruled out. Wilson is a WR2 this week.

 Wide Receiver 
 #5 
 Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said he is “confident” that Garrett Wilson (concussion) will play in Week 10 against the Bills. 
 Glenn said Wilson has one more step to clear before he is out of the league’s concussion protocol. Wilson missed last week’s game against the Chiefs due to his brain injury, but has practiced in a limited capacity twice this week and is trending toward a return. We will get a final update on Wilson once he has officially cleared the protocol, but fantasy managers can start him as a mid-to-high-end WR2 in a game that could feature plenty of points against a high-powered Bills offense.

 Garrett Wilson (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice. 
 Wilson still needs to be officially cleared from concussion protocol to play, but two limited sessions have him with a real chance to be active in Week 10 after missing Week 9. If he can play, Wilson will likely be an upside fantasy WR2 against the Bills.

 ESPN’s Rich Cimini reports the 49ers and Chiefs “were interested” in Garrett Wilson ahead of the trade deadline. 
 The Jets made it clear they were not moving Wilson early in the process, so we can’t imagine trade talks between them and either team made it very far. Cimini notes that the Jets could revisit a Wilson trade in the offseason. Wilson told reporters earlier this year that he loves it in New York, but he loves winning more. The Jets haven’t done much of that since Wilson was drafted. This will be a storyline to watch in the offseason, though we suspect he’ll remain in New York for the foreseeable future.

 Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said he’s “very hopeful” Garrett Wilson (concussion) will play in Week 10 against the Bills. 
 Wilson was sidelined in last week’s loss to Kansas City with the head injury he sustained in Week 8. Omar Cooper, Jr. functioned as the team’s top receiver with Wilson sidelined while Adonai Mitchell couldn’t reel in any of his seven targets from Geno Smith. Wilson would be a top-24 option in Week 10 against Buffalo if he can return to action. The Bills secondary allows the 13th highest fantasy points per target to boundary wideouts this season.

 Jets declared Garrett Wilson, Tim Patrick, Nahshon Wright, Joseph Ossai, Trevin Wallace, Kohl Levao, and Blake Freeland inactive for Week 9 against the Chiefs. 
 Wilson suffered a head injury last week and did not practice this week as he remained in the NFL’s concussion protocol. Look for Omar Cooper, Jr. and Adonai Mitchell to see more routes and targets against a tough KC secondary. Mitchell is likely to function as the team’s top wideout with Wilson sidelined.

 Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Garrett Wilson (concussion) will not play in Week 9 against the Chiefs. 
 Wilson has not practiced this week and has now been ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Chiefs. Wilson has caught 43 passes for 527 yards and three touchdowns this season and saw 12 targets in last week’s loss to the Raiders. His absence means both Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper should see expanded roles, but both players will be hard to trust as anything more than WR3s against a stout Chiefs defense. In addition to Wilson, the Jets also ruled out LB Trevin Wallace (groin) for Week 9.

 Garrett Wilson (concussion) did not practice Thursday. 
 Wilson did not practice on Wednesday and will go down as a DNP today as well. He is a long-shot to suit up for the Jets’ Week 9 game against the Chiefs. His absence will free up targets for Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. The two have alternated spike weeks and zeroes over their past two games. Now both should have stable fantasy floors for at least one game.

 Jets placed Garrett Wilson in the NFL’s concussion protocol. 
 He was officially a DNP for Wednesday’s practice. Wilson sustained a head injury in Week 8 against the Raiders and now appears to be a long shot for Week 9. Wilson this season has accounted for 27 percent of the Jets’ targets and 38 percent of the team’s air yards. His absence would make both Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper flex-viable for Week 9, along with Mason Taylor. Cooper is coming off a game in which he saw no targets while running a route on 75 percent of the Jets’ drop backs. 
 Garrett Wilson 
 NYJ 
 Wide Receiver 
 #5 
 Garrett Wilson caught 6-of-12 targets for 83 yards in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders. 
 Fresh off a three-target fiasco that prompted trade request denials from the Jets’ No. 1 wideout, Wilson was jammed the ball early and often. It was a clear, intentional commitment from Geno Smith and the Jets’ coaching staff. It still couldn’t prevent Wilson from once again getting out-shined by one of his positional mates, this time Adonai Mitchell. AD contributed an explosive 7/142/1 on nine looks. That’s now three 100-yard performances by Jets wideouts over the past three weeks with zero of them coming from Wilson. He still commands the most defensive attention, making life easier for Mitchell and rookie Omar Cooper Jr. Despite those frustrations and Wilson’s relative struggles, he will remain a must start for Week 9 against the Chiefs.

 Tyjae Spears (knee) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Jaguars.
 Spears hasn’t played since Week 6 because of the knee issue. He practiced in full this week but was still listed as questionable on Friday. He should be good to go for pass-catching duties in a game that will likely see the Titans throw a lot. Spears is a low-ceiling FLEX play in PPR leagues this week.

 Boston will likely go through a workout in the morning to determine his status, but he appears to be on the right side of questionable for now. He was held out of the Browns’ first two practices of the week before getting in a limited session on Friday. Barring a setback ahead of kickoff, Boston is back in the WR3 mix for Week 10.

 ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Gardner Minshew suffered a torn UCL and will undergo season-ending surgery. 
 This was the expectation after Minshew severely injured his elbow in Week 9 against the Seahawks. His season is over after one incomplete start. Minshew threw for 354 yards and three scores in 2026. The surgery could sideline Minshew for over a year, meaning he may not play in 2027.

 ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Patrick Mahomes suffered a “very small sprain of his UCL” and a muscle strain in Week 9 against the Jets. 
 Mahomes’ right arm was clobbered by a Jets defender while attempting to throw a pass late in the first half of Week 9. It looked like a serious issue at first, but he managed to finish the game and didn’t even miss any practice time this week. Per Schefter, the Chiefs consulted with physicians from the Rangers and Royals, who are among the world’s best doctors when it comes to shoulder and elbow injuries. Both doctors cleared him to play.

 Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is active for Week 10 against the Lions.
 There’ll be no Corey Kiner SZN then. I’ll tell the children. Stevenson is somewhat shockingly active after injuring his knee in Week 9. Initial reports had him missing multiple weeks. Instead, he’s good to go, though we should still expect Kiner to mix in for a few touches. Inactive for the Pats are QB Behren Morton, OG Ben Brown, OG Walter Rouse, OT Dametrious Crownover, CB Carlton Davis, and S Brenden Schooler.

 Rhamondre Stevenson is also active. Brown made the trip to Germany and was limited in all three practices this week. He has been dealing with knee issues for several years, and we’re sure this isn’t the last we will hear of it in 2026. Still, he has been cleared for action today, meaning fantasy managers should get him in their lineups. We’re treating him as a volatile WR2.

 NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Raiders planned to start Fernando Mendoza “in the next few weeks” even if Kirk Cousins had not been traded. 
 With games against the Seahawks and Broncos on tap for Mendoza’s first two starts, the Raiders may have wanted to throw Cousins to the wolves for those games before getting the No. 1 overall pick under center against Cleveland. Instead, the Vikings offered Vegas a third-round pick for Cousins and the Raiders couldn’t say no. Mendoza will make his first NFL start at home versus Seattle today. We expect him to be in the QB2 mix at some point this year, but it might take a few weeks given Vegas’s tough schedule. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak 
 Source:  Ian Rapoport

 NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Vikings have talked to Kirk Cousins “about returning to Minnesota for the 2027 season.”
 Rapoport notes that the Vikings told Cousins they wanted him around beyond this year before their trade for him was complete. They would go on to pay a third-round pick to reunite with their former starter. Even if Cousins is far from a superstar quarterback, head coach Kevin O’Connell is clearly sick of the weekly carousel under center. The Vikings will be legitimate Super Bowl contenders if Cousins can just play as well as he did in Vegas. A deep playoff run will all but guarantee him a spot on the roster next year. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak 
 Source:  Ian Rapoport

 Phillips hasn’t played since Week 6 because of the hamstring issue. One of Carolina’s biggest offseason additions, Phillips was off to a solid start to the year before going down. He had 2.5 sacks in five games, two of which he left early. Getting Phillips back will be a big win for the Panthers’ defense.
